title: What Does It Mean When a Guy Says...? 25 Phrases Explained — cv.cm
description: What guys mean when they say "Let's see where it goes", "I'm bad at texting" or "I'm not ready": 25 phrases, what each may mean and what to do next.
h1: What does it mean when a guy says...?
answer: Most phrases can mean more than one thing; his actions over the next weeks tell you which. "I'm not looking for anything serious" usually means exactly that. "I'm bad at texting" is fine if he still makes plans. "You're too good for me" is often a soft no. If you are unsure, ask him once, calmly, and believe what he says.

body: This page says "guys" because that is what people search. Men are not one type, and the same phrases mean much the same things when a woman, or anyone else, says them. A careful, honest man may say "Let's take it slow" and mean it as respect. Another may use the same words to avoid commitment. You learn which by watching what he does next.
Three rules for reading any phrase:

ol: Believe clear statements. When someone tells you what they do not want, it is usually true, even if they act warm.
Check words against effort. Kind words with no plans, no follow-up and no change mean less than they sound.
When unsure, ask once, kindly, and accept the answer.

body: Text makes all this harder. Research on email found that writers think their tone comes across much better than it does. A short "lol" may be warm, bored or tired, and you cannot see which. Do not build a story from one message.

sections.h: Relationship talk, soft no and warning phrases

head: Phrase
What it may mean
Depends on
What to do
rows: "I'm not looking for anything serious"
He does not want a committed relationship, at least now
Almost nothing: believe it
If you want something serious, say so and step back. Do not wait for him to change
"Let's see where it goes"
He is open but unsure, or he wants to avoid a label
Whether things move forward over weeks
Agree to a short time, then ask again: "Where do you see this going?"
"Let's take it slow"
Respect for your pace, or hesitation about commitment
Whether he stays in steady contact while going slowly
Ask what slow means to him, and say what you need
"I need time"
He is unsure or overwhelmed; can come before a breakup
Whether he says how long and stays kind
Ask once how long. Give the time. Do not chase
"I'm not ready"
Not ready for a relationship now, or not with you
Whether he acts like a partner anyway
Believe it. If you want a relationship, look after yourself and step back
"I just got out of something"
He is still hurt from a past relationship
How recent it was, and whether he still talks to the ex
Go slowly or step back. You cannot speed up his healing
"You're too good for me"
Usually a soft no; sometimes real low self-esteem
Whether it comes after you asked for more
Take it as a no. You do not need to convince him
"I don't want to hurt you"
He knows he cannot give what you want
Whether it comes with a clear decision
Believe him. This is often a warning, given kindly
"Let's stay friends"
No to romance
Whether you can be friends without hoping
Accept it. Decide honestly if you need distance
"I'm bad at relationships"
He expects to fail, or wants to lower your hopes in advance
What he does to change it, if anything
Listen. It is a statement about what he expects to give
"My ex was crazy"
The breakup was painful, or he blames others for problems
Whether he says this about many people, and whether he takes any share of blame
Listen to how he talks about past partners; it often shows how he will talk about you

sections.h: Why "You're different from other girls" is not a compliment
body: It sounds sweet, and he may mean it kindly. But the line praises you by putting other women down. It suggests most women are a problem and you are the exception, for now. It also puts pressure on you to stay "not like the others", which can mean not having needs, not getting upset and not asking for much.

A real compliment is about you, not a comparison: "I love how you think about things" or "You make me laugh more than anyone." If he says the "different from other girls" line, it is worth noticing how he talks about women in general. If you want to answer, keep it light and honest: "Thanks. I actually like most other girls."

sections.h: "Not serious", "see where it goes": how to get a clear answer
body: Vague phrases about the future are the most common source of confusion. They often lead to a situationship: something with feelings but no labels, plans or clear boundaries. Cleveland Clinic psychologists describe this as a relationship that has not been formalized, with sporadic contact and no talk about the future. See cv.cm's slang dictionary for what situationship means.
If you want clarity, ask for it in a calm, private moment:

ul: "I like you, and I'm looking for something serious. Is that something you want?"
"When you say let's see where it goes, what do you picture in a month or two?"
"I'm okay with going slowly, but I need to know we're going in the same direction."

body: Then listen. A clear no is painful but useful. A vague answer followed by the same pattern for weeks is also an answer. You can close kindly: "I've really enjoyed this, but I want something more steady, so I'm going to step back." If his attention comes in small, irregular pieces that keep you hoping, read the article on breadcrumbing.

sections.h: How to ask what he meant

ol: Choose a calm moment, not during an argument or at 2 a.m.
Repeat his words, without blame: "Earlier you said you need time."
Ask an open question: "What does that look like for you? A few days, or more?"
Say what you need, too: "I can give you space, but I'd like us to talk again by next weekend."
Accept the first clear answer. Do not keep asking in new ways.

body: Avoid tests: going silent to see if he chases, making him jealous, or checking his phone or social media to find the "real" answer. They create more confusion and hurt trust. If his words leave you anxious most of the time, the mixed signals and attachment styles articles may help you see the pattern.

ul: Hearing "not serious" and hoping your patience will change his mind.
Treating kind compliments as promises. "You're beautiful" is not "I want a relationship".
Explaining away low effort with "he's just bad at texting" for months.
Arguing with a soft no. If he says "You're too good for me", you do not need to prove you are not.
Assuming every man means the same thing by the same words.

body.note: If someone's words make you feel afraid, controlled or small, that is more than mixed meaning. Read the red flags article, and talk to someone you trust.

body: For a fuller picture of how he talks, texts and acts, cv.cm's Does my crush like me test can help. For the same guide from the other side, see what girls mean when they say.

faq.q: What does it mean when a guy says he's not ready for a relationship?
faq.a: It usually means he is not ready now, or not with you. Believe it. If you want a relationship, it is better to step back than to wait for him to change.

faq.q: What does it mean when a guy says let's see where it goes?
faq.a: He may be open but unsure, or he may want to avoid commitment. Agree to a short time, then ask directly where he sees things going.

faq.q: Is "I'm bad at texting" an excuse?
faq.a: Not always: many people dislike texting. It is fine if he shows effort in other ways, like calls and real plans. If there is little effort anywhere, it is low interest.

faq.q: What does it mean when a guy says you're too good for him?
faq.a: It is often a soft way to say no, and sometimes it reflects low self-esteem. Either way, it is not something you can talk him out of.

faq.q: What does it mean when a guy says he doesn't want to hurt you?
faq.a: He usually knows he cannot give what you want. Treat it as an honest warning and decide what is best for you.

faq.q: Do good morning texts mean he likes you?
faq.a: They are a good sign of steady interest, especially when he also makes time to see you. Texts alone, without plans, mean less.
